items.title: Don Menza and Sam Noto interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clinton, New York, January 28, 1997
items.q: I’ve heard Pavarotti say, “I’m an interpretive artist.”

ctx.x: Well I think it’s interesting for the listener too, see now the reason you’re saying that, like it did, it rang something in your brain, right?

Pushed a button. That’s what the music is supposed to do. It’s not supposed to be just one way all the time. That’s what he’s talking about that same solo thing. I mean I don’t know how anybody can do that. I don’t remember what I played the last time anyway. What’s the point. Even with great classical players. I’ve heard Pavarotti say, “I’m an interpretive artist.” He’s taken this and I think that’s what put him over the edge as far as popularity is that he just doesn’t go out there and sing it like all the…
Well this has really been fascinating. You guys have given us some great stories. I didn’t get to ask you about your L.A. days too much, but you had—
